text: Git branching helps developers work on different tasks without affecting the main code. A common practice is to create feature branches, where each new feature or fix is developed separately. Once the work is finished, you can merge the branch back into the main branch. Before merging, teams often open pull requests so others can review the changes and discuss them. This creates a clear version control workflow: create a branch, make changes, review, and merge. By following this process, teams avoid conflicts, keep the main branch stable, and make collaboration much easier and safer.
